name: Botch
label: Hydra Head
lede: Four Tacoma high schoolers named their band out of a dictionary, made two albums for Hydra Head, and quit at the Showbox in 2002. In 2024, after a reunion, they quit there again, on purpose.

eras.title: A dictionary and a dad's van
eras.text: Seattle's hardcore scene files them under weird kids from Tacoma. The first records come out on World of Hurt, Threshold, Phyte and Excursion, and Verellen's father drives the van.

years.big: "We were viewed as new jacks and weird kids from Tacoma."
years.h: Tacoma high schoolers name a band out of a dictionary
years.p: Dave Knudson pitched Tim Latona at school; Dave Verellen sang and Brian Cook played bass. Cook, on how Seattle's hardcore scene saw them:
years.xp:
Cook has said Knudson lured him in with the promise of recording a Dead Kennedys cover. Tacoma Music History says Verellen became the singer because he had no instrumental abilities.

Verellen's father drove the early tours in his van, and John Pettibone of Undertow called them a "next-generation band."

years.h: Dave Verellen's father drives the first tour into Canada
years.p: Faction is a seven-inch on World of Hurt and Threshold. The tour behind it goes north in a van with Verellen's father at the wheel.
years.xp: The band then spent roughly four years as a garage band, putting out demos and EPs before any real label came calling.

years.h: The John Birch Conspiracy Theory lands on Phyte
years.p: A second EP, more jagged and math-brained than Faction.

years.cap: Poster for the 1998 tour with Jesuit and The Dillinger Escape Plan
years.h: A cover of 'O Fortuna' catches Aaron Turner's ear
years.p: Excursion Records puts both EPs plus 'Closure' on one disc, including Botch's take on Carl Orff's 'O Fortuna'. [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] of Hydra Head Records hears it and signs them.
years.xp: Excursion put the record out again as Unifying Themes Redux in 2002, with extra tracks from the Nineironspitfire and [[Murder City Devils|32705a3c-54cf-4e48-a3ab-2801157a09dc]] splits. Hydra Head reissued the Redux version in 2006 in orange, not the original blue.

eras.title: Two albums at Litho
eras.text: Turner signs them to Hydra Head and Matt Bayles records both albums at Studio Litho. Work lamps go up on stage, Dillinger Escape Plan shares the road, and Rkcndy gets its last show.

years.h: Turner puts six or seven grand into American Nervoso
years.p: Recorded in March 1998 at Studio Litho in Seattle with [[Matt Bayles|e294077f-71eb-401f-a36a-f2dbcbd75863]]; nine tracks, out on Hydra Head May 20.
years.xp: Bayles produced with the band. The 2007 reissue restored two opening measures of 'Hives' that had been lopped off in the original mastering.

years.cap: Botch with Jesuit and the Dillinger Escape Plan, end of tour, 1998
yt: Full set, Deja One, Tacoma, July 15, 1998
years.h: Botch turns halogen work lamps on the crowd
years.p: On the American Nervoso tour, Botch starts aiming the lamps at the audience, so faces light up and Verellen can watch the room react.
years.xp:
Wikipedia quotes Verellen saying the rig let him see people's reactions because their faces were "totally illuminated." The first headlining tour behind the album also had [[The Dillinger Escape Plan|1bc41dff-5397-4c53-bb50-469d2c277197]] and Jesuit on it.

The clip is a fan-shot full set from Deja One in Tacoma, July 15, 1998.

years.big: "This is about being buried under thousands of tons of molten lava."
years.h: Botch is the last band to play Rkcndy
years.p: Dave Verellen introduces the last song, per Louder. The October 1999 show, with The Blood Brothers, Playing Enemy and Kill Sadie, comes as the all-ages club waits for demolition to make way for a hotel.
years.xp:
It is the first show for We Are the Romans, days before the album's release. Tacoma Music History dates it to October 27.

Louder adds that the band was also on the cover of Seattle paper The Rocket around this time, walking away from the camera.

years.h: We Are the Romans arrives on Hydra Head
years.p: Tracked at Studio Litho with Bayles between June 29 and July 8, 1999. The title comes from closer 'Man the Ramparts'.
years.xp:
Verellen described the Roman theme as starting from a gladiator-ish feel and turning into commentary on American decline. Cook drew on J.G. Ballard's The Atrocity Exhibition. 'Frequency Ass Bandit' was a last-minute rewrite of 'Frequenting Mass Transit', from an earlier split.

Ten tracks, 52 minutes and 35 seconds.

years.h: Knudson's pitch to Turner rules out palm-muting and open-E power chords
years.p: Knudson promises Turner a heavy, aggressive record without the standard hardcore moves.
years.xp:
Cook has said the band drew on [[Chavez|c08d2dcd-3c9a-4e5c-b444-c48936de2707]], [[Don Caballero|b93697af-a318-417a-b16e-a9eb47fbe2f8]], June of '44 and [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]] rather than on other hardcore bands, and Louder says they called the result "evil math rock."

The clip is a live set from March 5, 1999, venue unidentified.

years.cap: Botch live in a club, c. 2000
years.h: Dillinger Escape Plan takes Botch to Europe
years.p: Botch tours Europe with Dillinger in 2000 and plays a smaller North American run, with well-attended Seattle shows in early 2000, per Louder.

eras.title: Done before it went sour
eras.text: Writer's block, the weight of following We Are the Romans, and a rift between Latona and Knudson. Knudson starts Minus the Bear, and Botch ends in June.

years.h: Botch plays Louisville's Krazy Fest 4
years.p: July 28 in Kentucky: [[Coalesce|3d722ad8-1986-4ce0-bc98-d0864ef625f2]], [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], Poison the Well and Harkonen share the bill.

years.cap: Verellen and Knudson on stage, c. 2001
years.h: Knudson starts Minus the Bear on the side
years.p: He forms [[Minus the Bear|c1e98e4a-4628-4c89-a7a6-0e0171600b05]] with Jake Snider, Erin Tate, Matt Bayles and Cory Murchy: gentler, lighter guitar music than Botch.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the softer material Knudson was writing among the reasons Botch came apart. Minus the Bear's Highly Refined Pirates came out on Suicide Squeeze in November 2002.

years.cap: Verellen held up over the crowd
years.h: A rift between Latona and Knudson ends Botch
years.p: The friction started during the We Are the Romans sessions. In February 2002 the band announces it is done.
years.xp: According to Latona, it was creative differences, not personal ones. Verellen said it was best to break up while they were on top rather than torture themselves. Writer's block and the weight of the last album played a part too.

years.h: An Anthology of Dead Ends arrives after the band is gone
years.p: Recorded at Litho in March 2002, the six-song EP is out October 15. Bayles called the sessions incredibly tense.
years.xp: Two songs are live and one was an unfinished riff. The closer, 'Afghamistam', leans on quiet vocals, piano and spoken word. Pitchfork gave the EP 4.5 out of 10, and the CD included a video for 'Saint Matthew Returns to the Womb'.
play: Saint Matthew Returns to the Womb

years.cap: Ticket stub, the Showbox, Seattle, June 15, 2002
years.h: Botch ends at the Showbox with The Blood Brothers
years.p: June 15, 2002, Seattle, with Harkonen and Playing Enemy on the bill. Ben Verellen and all of Playing Enemy join for 'Man the Ramparts'.
years.xp: The show was released as 061502 on December 5, 2006 through Hydra Head, a DVD of 14 songs plus an audio CD.

eras.title: The long afterlife
eras.text: Cook, Verellen and Knudson spread across other Seattle bands, Hydra Head reissues both albums and then closes, and the catalog moves to Sargent House.

years.h: Cook starts These Arms Are Snakes and joins Roy
years.p: Brian Cook forms [[These Arms Are Snakes|e95a296e-a34c-4496-9a7c-a95683d487b5]] in Seattle with Steve Snere. He also plays with Dave and Ben Verellen in the folk-rock band Roy, whose Tacomatose came out in 2003.

years.h: Bayles remasters both albums for Hydra Head
years.p: American Nervoso is remastered on July 7 and We Are the Romans on September 11, with demos and live tracks on the second disc of the latter.
years.xp: In September 2011 a repress of the vinyl reportedly sold through about 450 jackets in under 20 minutes.

years.h: Cook takes the bass chair in Russian Circles
years.p: He becomes bassist for [[Russian Circles|cca40a67-e959-46f8-a3f3-8a3f77d2da9e]], and later plays with Aaron Turner in [[Sumac|9b98f3ed-d24a-479e-bd15-97c16de9f13f]].

years.h: Verellen fronts Narrows and works as a firefighter
years.p: [[Narrows|3a9bf775-66f1-4299-b062-5cb0585d5672]], with Ryan Frederiksen, release a self-titled EP on Deathwish.

years.h: Sargent House takes the catalog after Hydra Head closes
years.p: Hydra Head went out of business in 2020. Sargent House acquires the full Botch catalog in October 2021, and the band denies the reunion rumors that follow.

eras.title: Back for two years, then done
eras.text: A song, a birthday party, two Showbox nights in February 2023, a US tour, Europe and Australia. The last show is at the Showbox again.

years.cap: Botch in a warehouse for the 'One Twenty Two' video, 2022
years.h: 'One Twenty Two' is the first new Botch song since 2002
years.p: Knudson writes the riff in lockdown as a solo idea, asks Verellen to sing, and it ends up a bonus track on the Sargent House reissue of We Are the Romans.
years.xp: Knudson has said he thought of Verellen because he knew the best hardcore singer ever. Cook said it was not meant to be a Botch song, but with all four of them on it, it felt right: "we just wrote a Botch song by accident." The track runs just over two minutes, and Matt Bayles mixed it.

years.h: Twenty years to the day after Anthology, Botch plays Bayles's party
years.p: On October 15, 2022, the band plays 'Saint Matthew Returns to the Womb' at a private party for Matt Bayles.
years.xp: The clip went viral. When the band announced the Showbox dates on October 20, the two February 2023 nights sold out in 13 seconds, per The Stranger.

years.h: Spanish Ballroom first, then two nights at the Showbox
years.p: Botch plays Tacoma on February 17 and Seattle on February 24 and 25, then a 14-date US tour from October to December.
years.xp:
Part of the Spanish Ballroom tickets were held for in-person purchase only. The fall tour's support acts included Denial of Life, Sandrider, Dreamdecay, Filth is Eternal, Haunted Horses and Erosion.

Per The Stranger, Latona is the only member who didn't start another band after the split.

years.h: A 14-date run through the EU and UK, then Australia
years.p: The March run includes three UK dates; Australia follows in May 2024.
years.xp: The UK dates were March 21 to 23, in Bristol, Manchester and London.

years.big: "It's been so good to close things off properly."
years.h: The Showbox again, 22 years to the day
years.p: Dave Verellen, to Kerrang!. Botch's last show is June 15, 2024, in the same room as the 2002 finale.
years.xp:
Knudson had said there was no more music on the horizon and the reunion would last a very finite time. Cook told Kerrang!: "Every band is going to end, eventually."

Verellen, on the old days: "You can't shoot fireworks out of your vehicle at other cars on the freeway these days."

years.h: The last show becomes a live album and film
years.p: A record and film of the June 15, 2024 Showbox show is announced for Sargent House on June 27, 2025.

sources.title: Louder: Botch, We Are the Romans
